subject: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aws-partner.com>, AWS Marketplace Support <mp-saas-support@amazon.com>

Subject: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Hi Laura / Marketplace team —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. We're finalizing the contract flow for Acme Analytics (RDW-2433-AWS) and I want to lock down two items before we move the Billing & Fulfillment integration into staging:

1) Usage signal mapping: which customer-provided signals do we need to emit to satisfy the entitlement check? We currently emit: user_count (active_users), api_requests_30d, and storage_gb. I attached a draft mapping (usage_mapping_v1.xlsx) showing the payloads we plan to send in the Metering Service API and the corresponding AWS entitlement fields.

2) Invoice dispute & reconciliation: Acme asked for a clear dispute window and a reconciliation playbook that preserves co-sell reporting. We sketched a proposed flow (attached proposed_dispute_flow.pdf) but need to confirm the buyer-facing timelines (e.g., 30 days to raise a dispute) and the technical signals for pro-rata adjustments when refunds are issued.

Could you confirm the minimal required keys for entitlement reconciliation and any AWS-side expectations for idempotency (dedup keys) on fulfillment notifications? Also, any constraints on the time window for updating usage (e.g., retroactive updates allowed within X days)?

If it helps, Rafael and Marissa can hop on a short call to go over the payload format. We're aiming to start sandbox metering calls the week of Nov 15.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aws-partner.com>

Cc: AWS Marketplace Support <mp-saas-support@amazon.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the level of detail. Quick answers inline below and I attached the official SaaS Metering payload spec link.

1) Required entitlement keys: customer_identifier (must match the marketplace customer id), sku_id, period_start, period_end, usage_quantity, and usage_type. For entitlement reconciliation you should also include an optional reference_id that we recommend be your internal invoice id or event id.

2) Idempotency: yes — include a dedup_token (UUID) per usage report. Marketplace will dedupe identical dedup_tokens for a given sku_id and customer_identifier.

3) Retroactive updates: allowed within 14 days of the period_end. After 14 days you can file an adjustment request but automatic acceptance is not guaranteed. Keep an eye on clock skew; timestamps should be ISO-8601 UTC.

4) Dispute window: marketplace standard is 30 days from invoice delivery to open a dispute. For co-sell deals, if your buyer asks for extended windows, we can accommodate but it requires updating the entitlement terms in the contract.

5) Refunds & pro-rata: Marketplace expects you to report negative usage events with the same dedup_token pattern but a negative usage_quantity and a reference to the original positive event id. Include a reason_code field for auditing.

Next steps: please update your spreadsheet to add the dedup_token and reference_id columns and re-submit. Rafael — if you can confirm the webhook ack semantics (200 vs 202) for fulfillment notifications that would be helpful.

Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/seller-fulfillment/doc/saas-metering

Best,
Laura Chen
Partner Solutions Architect, AWS Marketplace

Attachment: AWS_SaaS_Metering_Spec_v2.pdf (official spec)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Laura — thanks for the clarification. A couple of implementation questions from our infra/fulfillment side: 

- Webhook ack: do you recommend returning 200 OK immediately and queue the processing on our side, or does AWS expect synchronous validation before returning 200? In our current sandbox the marketplace sends POSTs and expects a 200 within 10 seconds to consider the delivery successful.

- Event ordering: for negative adjustments referencing original events, should we include the original dedup_token in an original_event_id field, or is it preferable to keep a separate cross_reference_id? We want to avoid confusion if the original event was already deduped on your end.

- Large-volume mapping: Acme may emit very large delta files (millions of events per day). Do you have recommended batching sizes or chunking patterns to avoid timeouts?

We'll update the mapping sheet and send a compact sample payload for your validation. If you have a sandbox endpoint we can push to that would speed validation.

Thanks,
Rafael
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Tom —

Looping you in with Laura and Rafael to confirm operational details for billing/disputes. Short summary of what AWS Marketplace requires and our recommended buyer-facing controls: 

- Dispute window: 30 days from invoice delivery (standard). We can negotiate for Acme to have a 45-day window, but that will require a contract amendment.
- Retroactive adjustments: technical updates allowed up to 14 days after period close; after that we can file manual adjustment requests with AWS Marketplace.
- Refunds: implemented as negative usage events; refunds will appear on the next invoice cycle unless processed as emergency credits (rare).
- Reporting cadence: we'll publish a reconciliation report to your billing contact by the 5th business day after month close.

Please confirm if Acme needs the extended dispute window; if so we can route to legal for an amendment. Rafael — we'll plan to run a scaled sandbox test the week of Nov 15.

Best regards,
Ben

Subject: Re: Usage signals mapping + invoice dispute process for AWS SaaS fulfillment

Thanks all —

Quick confirmations from Marketplace:

- Webhook ack: 200 within 10s is fine; if processing will take longer, respond 202 and we will retry delivery up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
- Large volumes: push via chunked uploads (recommended chunk size ~5k events) or use S3 bulk ingestion for very large deltas — we provide an ingestion job that reads signed S3 manifests for high volume sellers.
- Event cross-references: include original_event_id on adjustments and keep dedup_token stable per event. Using cross_reference_id is fine as an additional field but original_event_id is the primary key we use in the reconciliation UI.

I'll provision a sandbox endpoint and a signed S3 bucket for your team by Nov 9. If you share the sample payload Rafael mentioned, I'll validate it against the ingestion job and send back a short report.

Laura
Partner Solutions Architect, AWS Marketplace
AWS Marketplace Support: mp-saas-support@amazon.com
